National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Narender Singh Khatri & Another on 4 February, 2022

 STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION UTTARAKHAND
                         DEHRADUN

                    FIRST APPEAL NO. 123 / 2017

National Insurance Company Limited
Branch Office, Near Kohli Hospital Building
Haridwar Road, Rishikesh, Uttarakhand
through its Authorised Signatory at

Rajpur Road, Dehradun

1.    Sh. Narendra Singh Khatri S/o Sh. Balwant Singh Rawat

2.    State Bank of India

      Karnaprayag, District Chamoli, Uttarakhand

Sh. Deepak Ahluwalia, Learned Counsel for the Appellant
Sh. Pradeep Bartwal, Learned Counsel for Respondent No. 1
None for Respondent No. 2

Coram: Hon'ble Mr. Justice D.S. Tripathi, President
       Mr. Udai Singh Tolia,              Member-II

Dated: 04/02/2022

                               ORDER

(Per: Justice D.S. Tripathi, President):

This appeal under Section 15 of the Consumer Protection Act has been preferred against the impugned judgment and order dated 30.05.2017 passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Chamoli (in short "The District Commission") in consumer complaint No. 11 of 2014; Sh. Narendra Singh Khatri Vs. National Insurance Company Limited and another, by which the consumer complaint has been allowed and the appellant has been 2 directed to pay the insured amount of Rs. 3,38,760/- to respondent No. 1 - complainant together with interest @6% p.a. from the date of institution of the consumer complaint till the date of payment, besides Rs. 25,000/- towards mental agony & economic loss and Rs. 3,000/-

towards litigation expenses.

2. Facts giving rise to this appeal, in brief, are that according to consumer complaint, the complainant had purchased Mahindra Maxx vehicle bearing registration No. UK11-TA-0196, after taking loan of Rs. 3,60,000/- from respondent No. 2 - State Bank of India. The vehicle was insured with the appellant - insurance company through policy No. 462201/31/12/6300001835 for a sum of Rs. 3,38,760/- for the period from 17.08.2012 to 16.08.2013. The complainant had gone to Dehradun on 04.09.2012 and the vehicle was parked by its driver at the main gate of Kalawati Dharamshala, Dehradun. In the next morning, the vehicle was not found at the spot, where it was parked. It was searched, but in vain. F.I.R. at case crime No. 297/11/12 under Section 379 I.P.C. was got registered in Police Chowki Laxman Chowk, P.S. Kotwali, Dehradun on 05.09.2012. Simultaneously, the insurance company and the bank were informed through telephone regarding theft of the vehicle. Case was investigated and ultimately, Final Report was submitted by the concerned police station on 28.01.2013. The complainant visited the office of the insurance company time and again regarding his insurance claim, but no payment was made and ultimately, it was informed by the insurance company on 24.03.2014 that the claim is not supported by valid documents and information and claim was repudiated. The insurance company has committed deficiency in service. Hence, the consumer complaint.

3

3. The written statement was filed by the insurance company before the District Commission and it was averred that the vehicle in question did not possess valid fitness certificate on the date of occurrence, hence the insurance claim was not payable and the complainant was informed accordingly. The insurance company has not committed any deficiency in service. Hence, the consumer complaint is liable to be dismissed.

4. In the written statement filed by respondent No. 2 - State Bank of India, it was averred that the complainant had purchased the vehicle in question after taking loan from the bank and amount of loan is outstanding against the complainant. The bank is not responsible for any payment of insurance claim.

5. After giving opportunity of hearing to the parties, the consumer complaint was allowed by learned District Commission vide impugned judgment and order dated 30.05.2017 and the insurance company was directed to pay the amounts, as stated above. Being aggrieved, the insurance company has preferred this appeal.

6. None appeared on behalf of respondent No. 2. We have heard the rival arguments advanced by learned counsel for the appellant and respondent No. 1 and perused the record.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the vehicle in question was required to be properly registered under the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. There was no valid fitness certificate of the vehicle on the date of theft, hence the vehicle could not be treated to be properly registered under the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. The impugned judgment and order passed by learned District 4 Commission is against the settled principle of law and the same is liable to be set aside.

8. Learned counsel for respondent No. 1 submitted that the vehicle was parked at the time of theft and it was not being plied, hence fitness certificate of the vehicle is immaterial and repudiation of insurance claim was not justified. He further submitted that if the vehicle is not found to be properly registered under the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the insurance company can not repudiate the entire claim of the complainant, rather the complainant is entitled for payment of his claim on non-standard basis at 75% of the admissible claim.

9. It is admitted fact that the vehicle in question was insured by the insurance company for the period from 17.08.2012 to 16.08.2013. It is also admitted that loss caused to the vehicle on account of theft, was covered under the insurance policy. Theft of the vehicle on 04.09.2012, is also not disputed. Question to be determined is whether there was valid fitness certificate of the vehicle in question on the date of theft or not.

10. We find from the record that letter dated 24.02.2014 was sent by the insurance company to the complainant, requiring him to furnish the fitness certificate of the vehicle at the earliest. We also find from the record that the claim of the complainant was closed vide letter dated 24.03.2014 issued by the insurance company to him, on the ground that inspite of letters / reminders issued to the complainant, he did not furnish the required papers / documents. Accordingly, it is evident from record that fitness certificate of the vehicle required from the complainant, was not furnished by him to the insurance company. According to complainant, theft of the vehicle in question took place 5 on 04.09.2012. We further find from record that the fitness certificate of the vehicle in question was valid upto 01.09.2012. There is no evidence on record to establish that the aforesaid fitness certificate was got renewed by the complainant after 01.09.2012. Accordingly, there was no valid fitness certificate of the vehicle in question on the date of theft.

11. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the vehicle in question was required to be registered under the provisions of Section 39 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. Section 39 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is reproduced below:

"39. Necessity for registration - No person shall drive any motor vehicle and no owner of a motor vehicle shall cause or permit the vehicle to be driven in any public place or in any other place unless the vehicle is registered in accordance with this Chapter and the certificate of registration of the vehicle has not been suspended or cancelled and the vehicle carries a registration mark displayed in the prescribed manner:
Provided that nothing in this section shall apply to a motor vehicle in possession of a dealer subject to such conditions as may be prescribed by the Central Government."

12. Learned counsel for the appellant further submitted that no vehicle can be deemed to be validly registered, unless it carries a certificate of fitness. Learned counsel has drawn our attention to the provisions of Section 56 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, according to which, no vehicle can be deemed to be validly registered for the purposes of Section 39, unless it carries a certificate of fitness. Section 56 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is reproduced below:

6
"56. Certificate of fitness of transport vehicles - (1) Subject to the provisions of Secs. 59 and 60, a transport vehicle shall not be deemed to be validly registered for the purposes of Sec. 39, unless it carries a certificate of fitness in such form containing such particulars and information as may be prescribed by the Central Government, issued by the prescribed authority, or by an authorized testing station mentioned in sub-section (2), to the effect that the vehicle complies for the time being with all the requirements of this Act and the rules made thereunder:
Provided that where the prescribed authority or the authorized testing station refuses to issue such certificate, it shall supply the owner of the vehicle with its reasons in writing for such refusal."

13. As discussed above, the vehicle in question did not carry a valid certificate of fitness on the date of theft and, as such, the vehicle in question can not be said to be validly registered for the purposes of Section 39 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. Learned counsel for the appellant has relied upon the judgment and order dated 16.09.2016 passed by Hon'ble National Commission in Revision Petition No. 622 of 2013; Baghel Singh Vs. National Insurance Company Limited, in which it has been laid down that a transport vehicle can not be deemed to be validity registered for the purposes of Section 39 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, if it does not carry a certificate of fitness. Relevant paragraph No. 11 of the said judgment is reproduced below:

7
"11. A plain reading of the above Section shows that in the absence of a certificate of fitness, a transport vehicle shall not be deemed to be validly registered for the purpose of Section 39 of the Act, which deals with the registration of motor vehicles. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Narender Singh Vs. New India Assurance Company Ltd. (supra) observed that the absence of valid registration of a motor vehicle amounted to a fundamental breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, for which the repudiation of the claim was justified."

14. In the light of provisions of Section 39 and 56 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 as well as the law laid down by Hon'ble National Commission in the case of Baghel Singh (supra), we find force in the aforesaid argument advanced by learned counsel for the appellant that the vehicle can not be treated to be validly registered for the purposes of Section 39 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, as there was no valid fitness certificate of the vehicle on the date of theft.

15. Learned counsel for respondent No. 1 submitted that the vehicle in question was parked at the time of theft and it was not being plied, hence claim of the complainant could not be repudiated by the insurance company. However, Hon'ble National Commission has laid down in its judgment and order dated 01.09.2016 rendered in Revision Petition No. 1264 of 2014; Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. and another Vs. Vikram Kanda, that it is immaterial whether the vehicle is parked or plying, rather it is mandatory that the vehicle should be validly registered under the provisions of Section 39 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. Relevant portion of paragraph No. 13 of the said judgment is reproduced below:

8
"..... Though, there is a specific pleading by the Complainant that the said vehicle was not used and was only parked at his residence as he was involved in some marital disputes, yet, the fact remains that no attempts were made by the Complainant in getting the registration extended. Irrespective of the fact, whether, the vehicle is parked or plying, it is mandatory that the vehicle be registered, as stipulated under Section 39 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988."

16. According to aforesaid law laid down by Hon'ble National Commission in the case of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. and another (supra), it is mandatory that the vehicle should be validly registered under the provisions of Section 39 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and it is not material whether it was parked or was being plied at the relevant time of theft.

17. Learned counsel for respondent No. 1 submitted that in the case of theft of vehicle, breach of condition of the insurance policy is not germane and the insurance company should have settled the claim on non-standard basis at 75% of the admissible claim. He has relied upon the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Nitin Khandelwal reported in IV (2008) CPJ 1 (SC). Paragraph Nos. 12 to 15 of the said decision are reproduced below:

"12. In the case in hand, the vehicle has been snatched or stolen. In the case of theft of vehicle, breach of condition is not germane. The appellant Insurance Company is liable to indemnify the owner of the vehicle 9 when the insured has obtained comprehensive policy for the loss caused to the insured. The respondent submitted that even assuming that there was a breach of condition of the insurance policy, the appellant Insurance Company ought to have settled the claim on non-standard basis. The Insurance Company cannot repudiate the claim in toto in case of loss of vehicle due to theft.
13. In the instant case, the State Commission allowed the claim only on non-standard basis, which has been upheld by the National Commission. On consideration of the totality of the facts and circumstance in the case, the law seems to be well settled that in case of theft of vehicle, nature of use of the vehicle cannot be looked into and the Insurance Company cannot repudiate the claim on that basis.
14. In the facts and circumstances of the case, the real question is whether, according to the contract between the respondent and the appellant, the respondent is required to be indemnified by the appellant. On the basis of the settled legal position, the view taken by the State Commission cannot be faulted and the National Commission has correctly upheld the said order of the State Commission.
15. The State Commission has allowed only 75% claim of the respondent on non-standard basis. We are not deciding whether the State Commission was justified in allowing the claim of the respondent on non-standard basis because the respondent has not filed any appeal against the said order. The said order 10 of the State Commission was upheld by the National Commission."

18. Considering the facts and circumstances of this matter; evidence available on record and law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the aforesaid case of National Insurance Company Ltd. (supra), the respondent No. 1 - complainant is entitled for the claim on non-standard basis, which will be 75% of the admissible claim.

19. For all the reasons mentioned hereinabove, the appeal deserves to be partly allowed and the impugned judgment and order passed by learned District Commission is liable to be modified accordingly.

20. In view of above, appeal is partly allowed. Impugned judgment and order dated 30.05.2017 passed by learned District Commission is modified to the extent that the insured amount of Rs. 3,38,760/- awarded by learned District Commission, is hereby reduced to Rs. 2,54,070/- (75% of Rs. 3,38,760/-). Remaining part of the impugned judgment and order passed by learned District Commission is hereby confirmed. Costs of the appeal made easy. 

      (U.S. TOLIA)               (JUSTICE D.S. TRIPATHI)
        Member-II                       President

K
